text: {"status":"CONFLICT","claims":[{"text":"The Acceptable Use Policy says employees may store Internal information in a personal cloud-storage account when working remotely if the account has multi-factor authentication.","evidence_id":"E1","quote":"Employees may store Internal information in a personal cloud-storage account when working remotely, provided the account is protected with multi-factor authentication."},{"text":"The Data Loss Prevention Policy says uploading company information classified Internal or above to a personal cloud-storage account is prohibited.","evidence_id":"E2","quote":"Uploading company information classified Internal or above to a personal cloud-storage account, such as a personal Dropbox, personal Google Drive or personal OneDrive, is prohibited."}],"conflict_evidence_ids":["E1","E2"],"conflict_note":"E1 permits storing Internal information in personal cloud storage when working remotely if multi-factor authentication is used, while E2 prohibits uploading company information classified Internal or above to personal cloud-storage accounts."}
